source.title: Noise-Driven Exploration and Transient Freezing Select Flat Minima in Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Ning Yang; Yikuan Zhang; Q. Ouyang; Chao Tang; Yuhai Tu

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and appendices, though it refers to supplemental material not included here.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiments on SGD noise, solution flatness, and test performance using continuation training and endpoint measures. These findings bear on the broader claim about training conditions and generalization, but do not test a listed version's specific setup and measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports trends in continuation test loss and flatness, freezing time, endpoint spread and flatness, and best-of-repeats test accuracy. It does not report random-label training, width sweeps, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons, adaptive optimizer comparisons, fixed-epoch large-batch comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The cited results of other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports SGD exploration, freezing, Hessian flatness, and test performance, but none measures a listed version. Batch-size comparisons use converged endpoints without an established fixed epoch budget (V5); Hessian flatness is neither magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness nor a measure of the training–test error gap (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute flat-valley selection to anisotropic noise and delayed freezing. Their theory distinguishes weaker fixed-location steady-state preference at higher noise from stronger final flat-valley selection caused by longer exploration.
record.recipe_differences: Studies SGD learning dynamics through checkpoint continuation, endpoint similarity, Hessian-based flatness, and a two-valley stochastic model; it does not use the interventions or measures specified in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and batch size change effective SGD noise, normalized freezing time, endpoint radius, final flatness, and best-of-repeats test accuracy. The continuation-time endpoint trends are reported for B=50 and η=0.05.

fits_no_version.finding: Later deterministic continuations from SGD checkpoints have lower endpoint test loss and greater Hessian flatness; these trends weaken after freezing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early SGD exploration reaches progressively flatter endpoints with lower test loss before basin commitment.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger SGD noise delays normalized freezing and produces greater endpoint spread and mean final flatness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD noise prolongs exploration and broadens access to flatter solutions.

fits_no_version.finding: Best-of-repeats endpoint test accuracy improves with stronger noise, with only weak accuracy variation overall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stronger noise can improve the best test accuracy selected across converged repeats in this MNIST experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger noise delays freezing and increases final flat-valley selection in the constructed two-valley model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise-delayed freezing can increase selection of a flatter valley in a landscape with Hessian-aligned noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Simulated ensemble flat-valley occupancy exceeds the equilibrium reference and eventually stops evolving; the theory predicts enhanced steady-state occupancy during active exploration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anisotropic noise biases valley occupancy toward flatter regions before transient freezing fixes the final distribution.

record.problems: The primary neural-network experiments are on MNIST with a multilayer perceptron; test accuracy varies only weakly across the small task. The paper refers to supplementary results and methods that are not included in the supplied text. It reports trend descriptions for several plotted quantities without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported qualifying results were left out. Cited findings from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning regimes.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance at fixed epoch budgets and recipe-dependent recovery.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness versus training–test error gaps and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. States are cannot_determine relative to those versions, without disputing the reported dynamics. Supplemental experiments and detailed training protocols are referenced but absent from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
Although batch size is varied, the paper does not test held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget against smaller batches.

The paper measures Hessian-based flatness and test loss/accuracy, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or the training-test error gap, and does not compare against the stated norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Measured test loss and Hessian-based flatness at deterministic full-batch GD continuation endpoints branched from different SGD checkpoint times.
rows.measure: Endpoint test loss and flatness; the text reports lower test loss and higher flatness for later continuation starts.
rows.value: Later continuations progressively land in valleys with lower test loss and higher flatness.
rows.note: The authors say late-time test-loss increases during continuation do not indicate worsening generalization because test accuracy has plateaued; they attribute the loss rise to increasingly extreme output logits.
rows.check: The reported trend is supported, but unscaled Hessian flatness versus test loss cannot establish V7.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Compared continuation endpoints across checkpoint times using Jaccard similarity of misclassified test sets, and measured endpoint test loss and flatness.
rows.measure: Endpoint test loss and flatness as continuation time approaches and passes mean freezing time.
rows.value: Endpoint test loss decreases and endpoint flatness increases as continuation time approaches and passes the mean freezing time; after the transition both vary more weakly.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars denote standard error of the mean (SEM).
rows.note: The paper defines freezing using mutual similarity of subsequent continuation endpoints and states the definition is robust to the similarity threshold.
rows.check: Endpoint similarity and flatness/test-loss trends around freezing do not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate and batch size and measured normalized mean freezing time across independent SGD runs.
rows.measure: Normalized freezing time η⟨tf⟩ relative to effective noise scale η/B.
rows.value: Across stochastic settings with B < 1000, normalized freezing time η⟨tf⟩ increases with effective noise scale η/B.
rows.note: The paper says η rescales iteration number to optimization time.
rows.check: Freezing time is a dynamics measure, not held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate and batch size and measured the RMS radius of converged endpoints across repeats.
rows.measure: Across-repeat RMS radius rθ of converged endpoints.
rows.note: The text describes this as a broader set of accessible endpoints.
rows.check: Endpoint spread does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate and batch size and measured mean final flatness among the same converged repeats used for endpoint spread.
rows.value: The same ordering is observed for mean final flatness as for endpoint radius; stronger-noise settings are associated with flatter endpoints.
rows.note: The paper does not give numerical cell values in the supplied text.
rows.check: Mean Hessian flatness alone establishes neither V5 nor V7.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Compared the best test accuracy across repeats for learning-rate and batch-size settings.

conditions.value: gray cells indicate settings with no final-converged repeats

rows.value: The paper reports improved best-of-repeats test accuracy with stronger noise, while test accuracy varies only weakly in this small task.
rows.note: The text does not provide numerical accuracy values.
rows.check: This is test-selected best-of-repeats accuracy among converged runs, not typical held-out performance. Flag as a selection statistic; no fixed epoch comparison establishes V5. Weak accuracy variation does not justify a partial state for any listed version.

rows.subject: two-valley model
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate η and noise strength σ in simulations and measured normalized freezing time and probability of convergence to the flatter valley.

conditions.value: half initialized on sharper side and half on flatter side

rows.measure: Normalized mean freezing time η⟨tf⟩ and probability Pflat of converging to the flatter valley.
rows.value: Normalized freezing time increases systematically with η and σ; Pflat rises sharply as η or σ increases.
rows.uncertainty: Fig. 3 caption says statistics were collected from 2000 simulations; no error bars stated.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a minimal model; its valleys have equal depth and different flatness.
rows.check: The subject is a constructed two-dimensional loss landscape, not a neural network with measured generalization. Freezing time and valley selection fit no listed version.

rows.subject: two-valley model
rows.operation_detail: Compared the simulated steady-state flat-valley probability with the equilibrium reference as a function of y and effective noise strength.
rows.measure: Steady-state flat-valley probability Pflat(y) relative to equilibrium reference Pflat^eq.
rows.value: The ensemble probability Pflat(y) stays above the equilibrium reference throughout the reported simulation.
rows.note: The authors distinguish this fixed-y steady-state result from the transient final-selection result.
rows.check: Fig. 4(b) reports an evolving ensemble occupancy that eventually freezes, not a steady-state measurement throughout. The fixed-y steady-state prediction applies during active exploration. Neither quantity measures a listed version.
